intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry, and you can stroll through historic courtyards, watch the royal guard-changing ceremony, and visit the National Folk Museum inside the palace grounds.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest traditional market and feast on iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant, bustling atmosphere of an authentic Korean market.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Take a professional K-pop dance lesson at one of Hongdae's popular dance academies such as Def Dance Skool or K-Arts Academy. Learn choreography from trending idol groups, get insider tips from trained instructors, and immerse yourself in the heart of Seoul's youth K-culture scene in the vibrant Hongdae arts district.

experiences.name: Bukchon Hanok Village & Traditional Tea Ceremony
experiences.description: Wander through the beautifully preserved alleyways of Bukchon Hanok Village, home to hundreds of traditional Korean hanok houses. Visit a local tea house for an authentic Korean tea ceremony experience, learning about the philosophy of darye (tea etiquette) while sipping on premium green tea and tasting traditional rice sweets.

experiences.name: Myeongdong Night Food Crawl & K-Beauty Shopping
experiences.description: Spend an evening exploring Myeongdong's legendary street food stalls offering tornado potatoes, lobster grilled cheese, Korean corn dogs, and hotteok (sweet pancakes). After eating, browse the dense concentration of K-beauty flagship stores including Innisfree, Etude House, and Olive Young to pick up cult skincare and makeup products at local prices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong Station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or a hot dog (under ₩3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just check in and rest. Exchange some cash at the airport (Incheon has competitive rates). Buy a T-money transit card (₩2,500) at any airport convenience store. Dress warmly; December temperatures hover around 3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse affordable K-fashion, accessories, and street snacks. Great way to ease into Korean shopping culture without spending much.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) to Incheon's Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Walk through the colorful Chinatown murals and archways, then explore Sinpo Market — a traditional market famous for local street food. Visit the nearby Open Port Area with its historic Japanese and Chinese concession buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Incheon's Songwol-dong Fairy Tale Village — a whimsical neighborhood with murals and sculptures, beautifully lit at night. Return to Bupyeong for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby Paris Baguette bakery (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Sinpo Market street food — try Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet fried chicken) and hotteok (sweet pancakes) (₩3,000–6,000)
meals.dinner: Bupyeong local pojangmacha (street food tent) — tteokbokki, sundae, and eomuk (fish cake soup) (₩5,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown is about 15 minutes by subway (Line 1, Incheon Station). Wear layers — it will be cold. Most underground markets are heated, making them perfect winter destinations.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Seoul via subway (Line 1 from Bupyeong to Seoul Station, ~50 min, ₩1,550). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early for the 10:00 Royal Guard Changing Ceremony. Admission is ₩3,000 (free with hanbok rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village — a traditional Korean village with hundreds of preserved hanok houses. Explore the narrow alleyways and enjoy free photo opportunities. Then visit nearby Insadong Street for traditional crafts, tea houses, and K-culture souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an indie shopping courtyard with local artisan shops and street performances. Browse affordable K-culture goods and handmade crafts.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong traditional restaurant — bibimbap or doenjang jjigae set meal (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market (short subway ride) — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare) (₩5,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is free on the last Wednesday of each month. Hanbok rental near the palace costs ₩10,000–15,000 and grants free palace entry. Gwangjang Market is one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets — a must for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden tour (₩8,000) is one of Seoul's most beautiful cultural experiences, especially with winter frost on the traditional pavilions. Book tickets in advance online.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Jongno-gu's Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendy neighborhood with cafes, vintage shops, and Korean street food set inside restored hanok buildings. Very photogenic and popular with young Koreans.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully lit urban stream running through central Seoul. In December, the Seoul Lantern Festival decorations may still be visible. Walk the stream path and enjoy the illuminated cityscape.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store kimbap and coffee (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong cafe or small restaurant — tteokbokki or Korean fusion (₩7,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha alley — grilled skewers, makgeolli (rice wine), and pajeon (green onion pancake) (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours run at set times and require advance booking — check the Cultural Heritage Administration website. Ikseon-dong is very Instagram-worthy and free to explore. The Cheonggyecheon Stream walk is completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Namdaemun Market — Seoul's largest traditional market, open since 1414. Browse affordable clothing, accessories, Korean snacks, and household goods. Great for budget shopping and experiencing authentic Korean market culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Myeongdong — Seoul's famous shopping and K-beauty district. Sample free street food from vendors (tteokbokki, corn dogs, lobster tails) and browse K-beauty stores like Innisfree, Etude House, and The Face Shop for affordable skincare.
day_by_day.evening: Take the cable car or hike up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) for panoramic night views of Seoul. The observation deck costs ₩21,000, but the free outdoor plaza and love locks area are equally stunning and free.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — hotteok or galguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — corn dog, tteokbokki, and fish cake skewers (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja restaurant — famous kalguksu and mandu (dumplings), a Seoul institution (₩9,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong street food vendors are most active in the afternoon and evening. K-beauty stores often give free samples — stock up! The Namsan cable car costs ₩9,500 round trip; alternatively, take bus 02 or walk the trail (30 min uphill).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hongdae (Hongik University area) — Seoul's youth culture and indie arts hub. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and the Hongdae Free Market (weekends, weather permitting). Browse indie music shops and K-pop merchandise stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area — explore the trendy shopping streets and the beautiful Ewha campus. Then head to the Han River (Yeouido or Mangwon) for a winter riverside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening street performance scene. Catch buskers and street performers near Hongdae playground. Explore the many affordable restaurants and cafes in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae cafe — Korean-style breakfast toast or egg sandwich (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Sinchon area — dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) restaurant, a local specialty (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food and affordable restaurants — try samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a budget BBQ spot (₩10,000–15,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is extremely lively on weekends. Many K-pop entertainment company buildings (JYP, etc.) are nearby for fans. The Han River parks are free but very cold in December — dress warmly. Bring hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) — one of Korea's most unique cultural and historical experiences. Book a budget DMZ tour through Koridoor or similar operators (₩25,000–45,000 including transport). Visit the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel and Dora Observatory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the DMZ tour — visit Dorasan Station (the last train station before North Korea) and the DMZ Peace Park. Learn about the Korean War and the ongoing division of the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by late afternoon. Rest and explore the area around your hotel in Bupyeong. Visit a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a relaxing and authentic cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store before early departure (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Included in some DMZ tours, or packed lunch/convenience store near the DMZ (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Bupyeong local restaurant — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal (₩7,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours depart early (usually 7:30–8:00 AM from central Seoul). Book at least 2–3 days in advance. Bring your passport — it is required for entry. The jjimjilbang experience costs ₩8,000–15,000 and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — great for warming up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the free outdoor areas and any current exhibitions. The surrounding Dongdaemun area has a rich history as a textile and fashion hub.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dongdaemun History and Culture Park — walk the ancient city wall remnants and learn about Seoul's history. Visit the nearby Heunginjimun Gate (Dongdaemun Gate), one of the original gates of Seoul's fortress wall.
day_by_day.evening: Dongdaemun is famous for its late-night wholesale fashion markets (open until 5 AM). Browse Doota Mall, Migliore, and the outdoor fabric markets for affordable K-fashion finds.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery near hotel (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a traditional restaurant, a warming winter dish (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun night market street food — tteokbokki, sundae, and hotteok (₩5,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: DDP hosts rotating exhibitions — check their website for current shows (some are free, some have a small fee). The Dongdaemun fashion markets are best visited in the evening and late night. Bring cash as many stalls prefer it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. Free to enter. Watch monks in their daily routines, admire the beautiful lanterns, and experience a moment of peace in the heart of the city. December often features beautiful winter temple decorations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Bukchon and Samcheong-dong area again at a leisurely pace, visiting any galleries or small museums you missed. Walk up to Bugaksan Fortress Wall for free panoramic views of Seoul (bring ID for registration at the gate).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square — the grand plaza in front of Gyeongbokgung Palace. Admire the statues of King Sejong and Admiral Yi Sun-sin, beautifully lit at night. The area is especially atmospheric in winter.

meals.breakfast: Samcheong-dong cafe — traditional sikhye (sweet rice drink) and patbingsu or warm baked goods (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: Samcheong-dong small restaurant — doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew) set (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area — affordable Korean restaurant or Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup, a Seoul classic) (₩15,000–17,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free and open daily. The Bugaksan Fortress Wall hike requires passport or ID registration at the entrance — it is a UNESCO-listed site. Tosokchon Samgyetang is a splurge but worth it for the cultural experience — it has been serving ginseng chicken soup since 1983.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks in Jamsil. Budget option: explore the free Lotte World Mall and the outdoor Magic Island area without buying a park ticket. The Christmas decorations are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Seokchon Lake — a beautiful free park surrounding Lotte World with stunning views of the castle and lake. In winter, the lake may partially freeze and the Christmas lights are magical. Visit the adjacent Songpa Naru Park.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city goes all out with lights and decorations. Head to Myeongdong or Cheonggyecheon for the festive atmosphere. Many churches hold Christmas Eve services open to visitors (Myeongdong Cathedral is stunning).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (₩2,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Jamsil area — affordable Korean restaurant or food court in Lotte Mall (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — splurge slightly on a Korean BBQ dinner in Myeongdong or Jamsil (₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World admission is ₩62,000 for adults — skip the park itself to stay on budget and enjoy the free surrounding areas. Christmas is widely celebrated in South Korea, especially in Seoul. Myeongdong Cathedral (Myeongdong Seongsang) holds a beautiful midnight mass — free and open to all.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Hanok Village — a free outdoor folk village with traditional Korean houses, cultural performances, and beautiful winter scenery. Experience traditional Korean games and crafts. The village is especially peaceful on Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Browse the diverse shops, vintage clothing stores, and multicultural restaurants. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (₩10,000) for world-class Korean and international art.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Gyeongui Line Forest Park (Gyeongui-seon Book Street) — a linear park built on an old railway line connecting Hongdae and Sinchon. Browse outdoor book stalls and enjoy the festive winter atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store Christmas special or hotel (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Itaewon — try affordable international food: shawarma, Indian curry, or Mexican tacos for a change of pace (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae area — Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at a local chicken restaurant, a beloved Korean tradition (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Many Korean businesses remain open on Christmas Day — it is a public holiday but celebrated differently than in Western countries. Namsan Hanok Village is free and a wonderful cultural experience. Itaewon has great vintage shopping for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Noryangjin Fish Market — Seoul's largest wholesale fish market, open 24 hours. Watch the early morning auction (best before 7 AM), browse hundreds of seafood stalls, and buy fresh seafood to have cooked at an upstairs restaurant for a fraction of restaurant prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yeouido — Seoul's financial and political island. Visit the National Assembly building exterior and walk along the Han River at Yeouido Hangang Park. In winter, the park is quiet but beautiful. Visit the IFC Mall for free indoor warmth and window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Yeongdeungpo Times Square Mall — one of Seoul's largest shopping complexes. Browse the CGV cinema, food court, and shops. Great for a warm, budget-friendly evening of people-watching and K-culture immersion.

meals.breakfast: Noryangjin Fish Market — fresh sashimi breakfast, a uniquely Korean experience (₩10,000–15,000 for a generous portion)
meals.lunch: Yeouido area — convenience store or affordable restaurant near the Han River (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Yeongdeungpo food court or local restaurant — japchae (glass noodles) or kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) set (₩7,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Noryangjin Fish Market: buy seafood from a vendor downstairs, then take it to a restaurant upstairs where they will cook it for a small fee (₩3,000–5,000 per dish). This is one of Seoul's most authentic and affordable food experiences. Arrive early for the best selection.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore any missed spots near Bupyeong. Visit a local jjimjilbang one last time for a relaxing Korean sauna experience. Pack souvenirs: affordable options include instant Korean ramen packs, dried seaweed, Korean snacks, and K-beauty products from Daiso (₩1,000 each).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Bupyeong Modoo Mall for last-minute souvenir shopping. Pick up Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts at Daiso (₩1,000 store) or the underground market. Check out of the hotel and store luggage if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Incheon International Airport via AREX or bus from Bupyeong. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Enjoy one last Korean meal at the airport food court.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery — final Korean breakfast (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Bupyeong market or convenience store — pack a kimbap roll for the journey (₩1,500–3,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport food court — bibimbap or bulgogi set for a final taste of Korea (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Daiso in Bupyeong Underground Mall is excellent for budget souvenirs. Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ₩500 card fee). The AREX from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport takes approximately 40–50 minutes. Check your airline's baggage allowance before shopping — Korean snacks and cosmetics can add up in weight!

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or a limousine bus to Bupyeong station area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store (GS25 or CU) near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or hotteok for a quick, affordable bite after arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly — December temperatures average around 3°C. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store or ticket machine for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some cash (KRW) at the airport for better rates. Rest well tonight as Day 2 begins your full exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a walk around Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center, one of Korea's largest underground markets. Browse K-fashion, accessories, and local goods. Get a feel for everyday Korean shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) from Bupyeong to Incheon Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Explore the colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion architecture, and the nearby Jayu Park — Korea's first Western-style park with great views of the port. Walk along the Open Port Area to see colonial-era buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Sinpo International Market for evening street food. The market is famous for Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken). Stroll the lit-up market stalls before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery like Paris Baguette — try a warm pastry and coffee (around 5,000–8,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) or tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork) at one of the authentic Chinese-Korean restaurants in Incheon Chinatown (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Sinpo dakgangjeong and tteokbokki at Sinpo International Market stalls (8,000–12,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers and a warm coat. The underground shopping center is a great way to stay warm while exploring. Bupyeong and Incheon Chinatown are easily connected by subway Line 1 — about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul via subway (Line 1 to Seoul Station, approx. 40–50 min). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Catch the 10:00 AM Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate. Rent a hanbok (traditional Korean dress) from a nearby rental shop to enter the palace for free and take stunning photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village, a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow alleys, enjoy the contrast of old architecture against the modern city skyline, and visit small craft shops and galleries. Continue to Insadong for a leisurely afternoon browsing antique shops, tea houses, and K-culture souvenir stores.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil — an open-air courtyard mall with indie shops, art installations, and street food. Enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store onigiri and coffee before departing.
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) near Gyeongbokgung — try bibimbap or doenjang jjigae at a local restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy restaurant in Insadong — try samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) at a mid-range BBQ spot (15,000–20,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental shops near the palace charge around 10,000–20,000 KRW for 2 hours. Bukchon Hanok Village asks visitors to be quiet out of respect for residents. Carry hand warmers — it will be cold walking outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower. Take the Namsan Cable Car up for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Visit the famous love lock fence and enjoy the crisp morning air. The tower area is magical in December with holiday decorations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and make your way to Myeongdong, Seoul's most famous shopping and beauty district. Explore K-beauty stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), fashion boutiques, and the lively street food scene. This is the heart of Korean pop culture commerce.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Myeongdong for the evening street food experience — one of the best in Seoul. The street vendors light up at night and the energy is electric even in winter.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the hotel or at a café in Myeongdong before heading to Namsan.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Myeongdong — try hotteok (sweet pancake), eomuk (fish cake skewers), and gyeran-ppang (egg bread) from vendors (5,000–10,000 KRW total).
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a Myeongdong restaurant — try naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles) or galbitang (short rib soup) to warm up (12,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower admission is around 21,000 KRW for adults. The cable car costs about 9,500 KRW round trip. Myeongdong is extremely popular — expect crowds on Friday evening. Olive Young is a must-visit for K-beauty products at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Seoul's most beautiful palaces, especially with winter frost on the traditional architecture. Book the Secret Garden tour in advance (guided tours only, limited spots).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Changgyeonggung Palace or head to the Jongno area to explore Tapgol Park and the traditional Jongno street. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns for the winter season.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic evening walk along the illuminated waterway. The stream is lit up beautifully in winter and is a peaceful escape from the busy city streets.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local sikdang (식당) near the hotel — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or congee (juk) (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Changdeokgung — try a warm sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local restaurant (9,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Jongno area — try dakhanmari (whole chicken in broth) at the famous Dakhanmari Alley near Dongdaemun (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours must be booked online in advance at the palace website. Tours are available in English. Wear very warm shoes as you'll be walking on stone paths. Cheonggyecheon Stream is free to visit and accessible from multiple subway stations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building. Visit the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. The area is fascinating for its blend of ancient city wall ruins and ultra-modern architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gwangjang Market, one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. This is a paradise for local food lovers — browse the fabric stalls and food hall packed with grandmothers cooking traditional dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dongdaemun for the famous night shopping experience. Dongdaemun's fashion malls (Doota, Migliore) open late and are buzzing on Sunday evenings. Browse K-fashion at wholesale and retail prices.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hotel — try a Korean-style egg sandwich and Americano at a local café (6,000–9,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Iconic lunch at Gwangjang Market — must-try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (addictive mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare). Budget around 10,000–15,000 KRW.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant near Dongdaemun — try gopchang (grilled intestines) or a hearty Korean stew (13,000–18,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: DDP admission varies by exhibition — check the website for current shows. Gwangjang Market is busiest at lunch and is a must for authentic Korean food culture. Dongdaemun shopping malls are open until 4–5 AM, so no rush in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk along the impressive 5.7 km fortress walls that encircle the old city. The winter scenery with frost on the stone walls is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (Hwaseong Haenggung) inside the fortress grounds. Visit the Suwon Traditional Culture Center to learn about local crafts and history. Browse the traditional market street near the fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Spend a relaxed evening near the hotel, exploring the local Bupyeong neighborhood — visit a jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a warm, relaxing evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store before departing for Suwon.
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — the city's most famous dish — at a local restaurant near the fortress (15,000–25,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Jjimjilbang restaurant or a nearby Korean restaurant in Bupyeong — try kimchi jjigae or budae jjigae (army stew) (10,000–15,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress admission is around 1,000 KRW. Take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong directly to Suwon Station (about 50 minutes). A jjimjilbang entry costs around 10,000–15,000 KRW and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — perfect for warming up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the epicenter of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals, quirky cafés, and K-pop culture shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area. The Ewha campus is architecturally stunning with its famous underground ECC building. Browse the trendy shops and cafés in Sinchon, popular with university students.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening — the neighborhood truly comes alive at night with buskers, live music, and street performances. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for an authentic K-culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Trendy café breakfast in Hongdae — try a Korean-style brunch at one of the many Instagram-worthy cafés (8,000–13,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hongdae — try tteokbokki and sundae (blood sausage) at a pojangmacha (street tent) or a casual restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Hongdae restaurant — try yangnyeom chicken (Korean fried chicken) with a cold Hite beer at a local chimaek spot (15,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Norebang rooms cost around 15,000–25,000 KRW per hour for a private room. Hongdae is very lively on weekday evenings — expect street performers even in December. The Trick Eye Museum costs around 15,000 KRW. Hongdae is accessible via subway Line 2 or the AREX airport line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon's multicultural neighborhood — browse the international restaurants, vintage clothing shops, and antique stores on Antique Furniture Street. Walk up to Haebangchon (HBC) for a more local, artsy vibe with independent cafés and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district for the evening. Visit COEX Mall — one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls — and the famous COEX Starfield Library, a stunning public library inside the mall. Browse the bookstore and enjoy the festive Christmas decorations.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local restaurant (9,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: International lunch in Itaewon — try a Korean-Mexican fusion burrito or a Middle Eastern shawarma for a multicultural experience (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gangnam — try a modern Korean restaurant or a trendy ramen shop near COEX (13,000–20,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum admission is around 10,000 KRW. COEX Starfield Library is free to visit and is one of Seoul's most photogenic spots. Gangnam is accessible via subway Line 2. The area will be beautifully decorated for Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park for a morning winter hike. The mountain park sits within Seoul city limits and offers spectacular views of the snow-dusted peaks and the city below. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Myeongdong Cathedral — Seoul's most iconic Catholic church, beautifully lit for Christmas Eve. The area around the cathedral will be festively decorated. Browse the Christmas markets and enjoy the holiday atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Christmas Eve in Seoul — the city goes all out with lights and celebrations. Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream or City Hall Plaza for the Christmas light festival. Many young Koreans celebrate Christmas Eve like Valentine's Day, making the city especially lively.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — convenience store kimbap and hot coffee or a quick meal near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Post-hike warm meal near Bukhansan — try a hearty doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae at a mountain restaurant (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — treat yourself to a Korean BBQ restaurant in Myeongdong or a nice Korean fusion restaurant (20,000–30,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is free to enter. Wear proper hiking boots and warm layers — trails can be icy in December. Bring crampons or ice grips for shoes if possible. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very romantic and festive — the city is beautifully illuminated. Book dinner in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (less crowded than Gyeongbokgung) and the Seoul Museum of History next door. Learn about Seoul's transformation from ancient Joseon capital to modern megacity through fascinating exhibits. The museum is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighborhood of traditional hanok houses converted into cafés, art galleries, and boutiques. This is a quieter, more authentic alternative to Bukchon. Visit the Yun Dong-ju Literary Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower in Jamsil for the evening. Visit the Sky Observatory on the 117th–123rd floors for breathtaking nighttime views of Seoul. The tower and surrounding Lotte World Mall are spectacularly lit for Christmas.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning café breakfast — try a festive holiday drink and pastry at a cozy Seochon café (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Seochon Village — try a traditional Korean meal at a hanok café-restaurant (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner near Lotte World — try a nice Korean or international restaurant in the Jamsil area (20,000–30,000 KRW).

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Museum of History is free. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory costs around 27,000 KRW. Many restaurants may have special Christmas menus — check in advance. Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea, so some smaller shops may be closed but major attractions remain open.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the largest museums in Asia, with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. The museum is free and takes 2–3 hours to explore properly. Don't miss the Goryeo celadon and Joseon white porcelain collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the War Memorial of Korea nearby — a powerful and moving museum documenting Korea's military history, including the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits with tanks, aircraft, and warships are impressive even in winter. Free admission.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your last full evening in the Yongsan Electronics Market or head back to a favorite neighborhood for final shopping and souvenir hunting. Visit a traditional Korean tea house for a warm, reflective end to your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near the hotel for a relaxed morning start.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Museum of Korea's cafeteria or a nearby restaurant — try a Korean set meal (10,000–15,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable Korean meal. Try a traditional Korean royal cuisine restaurant or a premium Korean BBQ spot (25,000–35,000 KRW per person).

day_by_day.notes: Both the National Museum of Korea and the War Memorial are free. The National Museum is closed on Mondays. Allow at least 2 hours for each museum. This is a great day for reflection on Korean history and culture before your trip ends. Pack souvenirs tonight to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely walk around the Bupyeong neighborhood. Visit a local juk (porridge) restaurant for a light, healthy Korean breakfast. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for affordable K-fashion and accessories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee experience. Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or limousine bus (allow 60–90 minutes from Bupyeong). Use remaining KRW at the airport duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of K-culture, incredible food, and unforgettable experiences in Seoul and Incheon.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — try juk (rice porridge) with various toppings at a local porridge restaurant (8,000–12,000 KRW).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — try a Korean meal at one of the many airport restaurants before departure (12,000–18,000 KRW).
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the hotel. Incheon Airport is one of the world's best airports with excellent shopping, dining, and cultural experiences (free Korean cultural performances and craft workshops in the transit area). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. T-money card can be refunded at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Wearing Hanbok grants free palace entry, and you can stroll through historic courtyards, watch the royal guard-changing ceremony, and visit the National Folk Museum inside the palace grounds.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest traditional market and feast on iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the vibrant, bustling atmosphere of an authentic Korean market.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Take a professional K-pop dance lesson at one of Hongdae's popular dance academies such as Def Dance Skool or K-Arts Academy. Learn choreography from trending idol groups, get insider tips from trained instructors, and immerse yourself in the heart of Seoul's youth K-culture scene in the vibrant Hongdae arts district.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked premium airport limousine or private transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Take a short walk around the Bupyeong area if energy permits – the neighborhood has convenience stores and late-night eateries open past midnight.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival snack: grab a warm bowl of instant ramyeon or kimbap from a nearby 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel, or order room service if available.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a KAL Limousine Bus or private chauffeur service from Incheon Airport to Bupyeong for a smooth, comfortable arrival. Journey takes approximately 50–70 minutes depending on traffic. Keep Day 2 light to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from jet lag. After a leisurely wake-up, explore the Bupyeong area on foot. Visit Bupyeong Modoo Mall underground shopping complex for a gentle introduction to Korean retail culture. Stroll through the Bupyeong traditional market alleyways to observe local morning life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Bupyeong Station, Line 1) into central Incheon and visit Incheon Chinatown and Jayu Park – a charming cultural enclave with colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion architecture, and the historic MacArthur statue overlooking the harbor. Walk across to Sinpo International Market for a taste of Incheon's own street food scene.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong by subway. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a premium Korean BBQ restaurant in the Bupyeong area. Try Hanwoo (Korean native beef) grilled tableside – a quintessential luxury Korean dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café – try a Korean-style breakfast set with doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew), rice, and banchan at a local sikdang (Korean diner).
meals.lunch: Sinpo International Market: try Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy fried chicken) and hotteok (sweet pancakes) – Sinpo is the birthplace of this style.
meals.dinner: Premium Hanwoo Korean BBQ at a reputable local restaurant in Bupyeong. Budget approximately ₩80,000–₩120,000 per person. Pair with premium makgeolli or soju.

day_by_day.notes: Keep the day relaxed and local. This is an orientation day to adjust to the time zone and get comfortable with the subway system before heading into Seoul proper.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Bupyeong to central Seoul via subway (approximately 50–60 minutes to Gyeongbokgung area). Begin the day with the Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience. Rent a premium Hanbok from a reputable rental shop near the palace gates (shops open from 09:00). Explore the grand Joseon-era palace grounds dressed in traditional attire – Hanbok wearers receive free palace entry. Visit Geunjeongjeon (the throne hall), Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village – a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow stone-paved alleys, admire the tiled rooftops against the winter skyline, and visit a small craft gallery or tea house. Afterward, head to Insadong for artisan shops, Korean craft boutiques, and cultural galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Insadong or Anguk area at a refined Korean traditional cuisine restaurant. Return to Bupyeong by subway.

meals.breakfast: Before departing Bupyeong, enjoy a warm breakfast at a local café or bakery – try a Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for a Korean-style pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) near Insadong – a multi-course spread of seasonal banchan, grilled fish, rice, and soup. Recommended: Sanchon or a similar heritage restaurant.
meals.dinner: Upscale Korean cuisine at Tosokchon Samgyetang (famous ginseng chicken soup) or a premium restaurant in the Anguk neighborhood. Budget ₩50,000–₩80,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly – December temperatures average 3°C and the palace grounds are exposed to wind. The Hanbok rental keeps you warm with layered traditional garments. Book Hanbok rental in advance during peak winter season.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) – Seoul's epicenter of youth culture, street art, and K-pop. Start with a morning walk through the Hongdae street art district and visit the Trick Eye Museum or a local indie gallery. Browse vinyl record shops and K-pop merchandise stores that open from 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a professional K-Pop Idol Dance Class at one of Hongdae's renowned dance academies such as Def Dance Skool or 1MILLION Dance Studio. A 90-minute to 2-hour session will teach you choreography from a popular idol group. This is an immersive, high-energy K-culture experience led by professional instructors.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae's vibrant nightlife district. Visit a premium cocktail bar or rooftop lounge for drinks, then enjoy dinner at a trendy Hongdae restaurant. The area is lively on Friday evenings with street performances and pop-up events.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a stylish Hongdae café – try Café Bora (known for purple taro lattes and Korean-inspired pastries) or a specialty coffee roastery in the area.
meals.lunch: Korean fried chicken and craft beer at a premium chimaek (chicken + maekju) restaurant in Hongdae – a beloved Korean cultural institution.
meals.dinner: Modern Korean fusion dinner at a well-regarded Hongdae restaurant. Try omakase-style Korean cuisine or a premium tasting menu. Budget ₩80,000–₩150,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the K-Pop dance class at least 2–3 days in advance as popular time slots fill quickly, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable athletic clothing and bring a change of clothes. The dance class typically costs ₩30,000–₩50,000 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market for the Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour – Seoul's oldest and most iconic traditional market, established in 1905. Arrive early (around 09:00–10:00) before the weekend crowds peak. Feast on bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), yukhoe (Korean beef tartare), and tteokbokki. Engage with the grandmothers (haenyeo) who have been cooking the same recipes for decades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) – Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Explore the design exhibitions, fashion pop-ups, and the surrounding Dongdaemun shopping district. Visit the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park for a glimpse of excavated Joseon-era ruins beneath the modern plaza.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic winter evening walk along the illuminated waterway. The stream is beautifully lit in December. End the evening with dinner in the nearby Euljiro or Myeongdong area.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market street food breakfast – bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and a warm bowl of kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup). Budget ₩15,000–₩25,000 for a full market breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near DDP or a quick Korean noodle dish (naengmyeon or kalguksu) at a nearby restaurant.
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at a Myeongdong or Euljiro restaurant. Try Myeongdong Kyoja (famous for kalguksu and mandu) or a high-end Korean restaurant in the area. Budget ₩60,000–₩100,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends – arrive early for the best experience and to secure seating at popular stalls. Bring cash as many vendors do not accept cards. The market is covered and heated, making it ideal for cold December days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Secret Garden tour (available in English, must be booked in advance) takes you through a stunning 78-acre royal garden with pavilions, lotus ponds, and ancient trees. In winter, the bare trees and frost create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jongno area – the historic heart of Seoul. Visit Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with lanterns in winter. Walk through Pimatgol Alley, a historic pedestrian lane with traditional eateries. Browse the antique shops and art galleries of Insa-dong.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performance – book tickets for a Nanta Show (non-verbal percussion performance) or a traditional gugak (Korean classical music) concert at the National Theater of Korea or Seoul Arts Center.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a hanok-style restaurant near Anguk Station – try a warm sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set with rice and banchan.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in the Jongno area. Try Jongno Haemul Pajeon (seafood scallion pancake) or a refined bibimbap at a heritage restaurant.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at a sophisticated Korean restaurant near the performance venue. Try a modern Korean tasting menu. Budget ₩100,000–₩180,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Garden tour at Changdeokgung must be booked in advance online (tickets sell out quickly on weekends). Tours run at specific times and last approximately 90 minutes. Dress in very warm layers as the garden is fully exposed to winter cold.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) – one of the most historically significant and unique experiences in Korea. Book a premium guided DMZ tour from Seoul (departs around 08:00–09:00 from central Seoul). Visit the Joint Security Area (JSA) at Panmunjom, the Third Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory, and Dorasan Station. This is a sobering and fascinating window into Korean history and the ongoing division of the peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the DMZ tour (most full-day tours return to Seoul by 17:00–18:00). The JSA tour requires advance booking through an authorized tour operator and passport registration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Itaewon or Hannam-dong – Seoul's most cosmopolitan neighborhood with a wide range of premium international and Korean dining options.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick café stop before the tour departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included in premium DMZ tour packages, served at a restaurant near the DMZ area.
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Hannam-dong or Itaewon. Try Gaon (a Michelin-starred Korean fine dining restaurant) or a high-end international restaurant. Budget ₩150,000–₩300,000 per person for fine dining.

day_by_day.notes: The JSA/DMZ tour requires passport registration at least 48–72 hours in advance. Book through a reputable operator such as USO Tours or Koridoor. Dress conservatively (no ripped jeans or revealing clothing) as per JSA regulations. Photography is restricted in certain areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Mountain and N Seoul Tower. Take the Namsan Cable Car up to the summit for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Visit the N Seoul Tower observation deck and add a love lock to the famous fence. The tower is beautifully illuminated in December. Explore the Namsan Hanok Village at the base of the mountain – five restored traditional houses with cultural demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myeongdong – Seoul's premier shopping and beauty district. Explore the flagship stores of Korean beauty brands (Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Laneige, Amorepacific). Visit the Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic-style landmark. Browse the outdoor street food stalls for afternoon snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Gangnam district in the evening. Visit COEX Mall (one of Asia's largest underground shopping malls) and the stunning COEX Starfield Library. Enjoy dinner in Apgujeong or Cheongdam-dong – Seoul's most luxurious dining and fashion district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a premium café in the Bupyeong or Incheon area before heading out.
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch – try egg bread (gyeran-ppang), tornado potato, and tteokbokki from the famous outdoor stalls. Budget ₩10,000–₩20,000.
meals.dinner: Upscale dinner in Cheongdam-dong or Apgujeong. Try Mingles (Michelin-starred modern Korean) or a premium Korean BBQ with premium Hanwoo cuts. Budget ₩150,000–₩250,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Namsan Cable Car can have queues in the morning – consider going early or purchasing tickets online. N Seoul Tower observation deck tickets cost approximately ₩21,000. Myeongdong is extremely busy on weekday afternoons – keep valuables secure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan – one of the largest museums in Asia with an extraordinary collection of Korean art, history, and artifacts spanning 5,000 years. Highlights include the Pensive Bodhisattva statue, Goryeo celadon ceramics, and the stunning 13-story Gyeongcheonsa Pagoda. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Itaewon and Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhoods – a multicultural enclave with antique shops, international restaurants, and a bohemian atmosphere. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art for world-class Korean and international contemporary art in a stunning building designed by Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium Korean spa (jjimjilbang) experience at Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan – a luxury multi-floor spa complex with various themed saunas, hot baths, and relaxation areas. A perfect way to warm up on a cold December evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near the National Museum or in the Yongsan area.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the National Museum's restaurant or a nearby Korean restaurant – try a premium dosirak (Korean lunch box) set.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Itaewon before heading to Dragon Hill Spa. Try a Korean-Western fusion restaurant or a high-end Japanese omakase in the area. Budget ₩80,000–₩150,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours and costs approximately ₩15,000–₩20,000 entry. Bring a change of clothes and toiletries. The spa provides uniforms (jjimjilbang clothes) for use inside. The Leeum Museum may have specific opening hours – check in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World – one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, located in Jamsil. Explore the indoor Magic Island and the outdoor Lotte World Adventure. In December, the park is decorated with elaborate Christmas displays and hosts special holiday events. Alternatively, visit the adjacent Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (123 floors, 555m) for breathtaking views of Seoul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jamsil and Songpa area. Visit Seokchon Lake Park, beautifully decorated with Christmas lights and winter illuminations. Browse Lotte World Mall for premium Korean and international brands.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration. Head to Myeongdong or Gangnam for the festive atmosphere – streets are decorated with lights and there are outdoor performances. Enjoy a special Christmas Eve dinner at a premium restaurant. Many upscale restaurants offer special holiday tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas Eve breakfast at a premium hotel café or bakery – try a special holiday pastry set.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lotte World Mall's premium food court or a restaurant in the Jamsil area.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a premium Seoul restaurant. Consider La Yeon (Michelin 3-star Korean fine dining at The Shilla Hotel) or a luxury hotel restaurant offering a holiday tasting menu. Book well in advance. Budget ₩200,000–₩400,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the busiest nights in Seoul – book dinner reservations at least 2–3 weeks in advance. The Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (Seoul Sky) offers stunning nighttime views and is particularly magical on Christmas Eve. Tickets cost approximately ₩27,000.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning in Seoul. Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (a quieter, less-visited Joseon palace) for a peaceful morning stroll. Nearby, explore the Seoul Museum of History for a fascinating overview of Seoul's transformation from ancient capital to modern megacity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the trendy Seongsu-dong neighborhood – often called 'Seoul's Brooklyn.' This former industrial district has been transformed into a hub of artisan cafés, design studios, and concept stores. Visit the Daelim Warehouse (a converted factory turned cultural space), browse independent boutiques, and enjoy the creative atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Banpo Bridge and Hangang Park for the evening. The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain (seasonal – check if operating in December) is a spectacular sight. Walk along the Hangang riverside and enjoy the winter cityscape. End with a warm dinner in the Banpo or Seocho area.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning brunch at a premium café or hotel restaurant – treat yourself to a Western-style brunch with eggs benedict, smoked salmon, and champagne.
meals.lunch: Artisan café lunch in Seongsu-dong – try a specialty coffee and a gourmet sandwich or Korean fusion dish at one of the neighborhood's concept cafés.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at a premium Korean or international restaurant in Seocho or Gangnam. Try Jungsik (Michelin 2-star modern Korean) or a luxury hotel restaurant. Budget ₩200,000–₩350,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions and restaurants are open on Christmas Day in Seoul as it is a public holiday but widely celebrated. Seongsu-dong is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood is particularly photogenic with its industrial-chic aesthetic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park – a stunning mountain park on the northern edge of Seoul. Take a moderate hiking trail (Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail recommended) through ancient fortress walls with panoramic winter views of the city. The snow-dusted peaks and frozen streams create a magical winter landscape. Allow 3–4 hours for the hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the Bukchon area again for any missed spots, or head to the Seodaemun Prison History Hall – a sobering but important museum documenting Korea's independence movement and Japanese colonial period. Afterward, explore the Sinchon and Ewha University area for shopping and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Seoul. Visit a premium rooftop bar for cocktails with a view – try Southside Parlor in Itaewon or a rooftop lounge in Gangnam. Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of Seoul's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike – a hearty Korean breakfast of doenjang jjigae, rice, and grilled fish at a local restaurant near Bukhansan.
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at a traditional Korean restaurant near the park entrance – try a warming sundubu jjigae or galbitang (short rib soup) to recover from the cold.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at a top-tier Seoul restaurant. Consider Kwon Sooksoo (modern Korean fine dining), Gaon (Michelin 3-star), or a premium Korean BBQ with the finest Hanwoo cuts. Budget ₩200,000–₩400,000 per person. Pair with premium Korean wine or aged soju.

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan hiking trails can be icy in December – bring microspike crampons or rent them at the park entrance. Start the hike early (by 08:00–09:00) to complete it before afternoon. The park is very popular on weekends so expect fellow hikers on the trails.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul/Incheon. Wake up early and enjoy a last Korean breakfast near the hotel. Do any final souvenir shopping in the Bupyeong area – pick up Korean beauty products, traditional teas, premium dried seaweed (gim), or Korean snacks as gifts. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private transfer or airport limousine from Bupyeong to Incheon International Airport (approximately 30–40 minutes). Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and security. Explore Incheon Airport's duty-free shopping – one of the world's best airport retail experiences with Korean beauty, fashion, and food products. Visit the Korean Cultural Street inside the airport for a final cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Enjoy the premium lounge facilities before boarding. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of K-culture, world-class cuisine, and unforgettable Korean experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast near the hotel – a comforting bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) or haejang-guk (hangover soup) with rice and kimchi.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Incheon Airport – try the premium Korean restaurant options in the departure terminal, or enjoy a final bibimbap or Korean BBQ set at one of the airport's sit-down restaurants.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport lounge dining before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for check-in, immigration, and security at Incheon Airport. The airport is large and efficient but can be busy on Sunday afternoons. Use any remaining Korean Won at duty-free or exchange back to your home currency at the airport exchange counters. Incheon Airport has excellent luggage storage and wrapping services if needed.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
